aging older monolingually-speaking English adults performed less well in terms of accuracy on conventional metaphors than the young monolinguists, and that bilingualism did not affect the performance of young and aging older adults.

the effects of aging and bilingualism on non-literal language processing in monolingual and bilingual adults.

the present study found no significant differences between monolingual and bilingual adults in terms of non-literal pragmatic inferences, but found that aging older monolingually English-speaking adults were less efficient than young monolingual adults in making pragmatic inferences of a particular type of non-literals (i.e. conventional metaphors).
bilingualism does not seem to be a significant factor in pragmatic inferences.
